extracted.intended_audience: neuroscience researchers and cognitive neuroscientists designing or evaluating fMRI studies of humor and sex/gender differences
extracted.subtask_description: Event-related fMRI investigation comparing neural responses to three types of verbal jokes (bridging-inference, exaggeration, ambiguity) versus baselines and contrasting women and men; includes behavioral ratings, ROI analyses, time-series and variance analyses, and random-group checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral funniness rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants were requested to rate the funniness of a joke on a 4-point scale (1 = not funny at all, 2 = not funny, 3 = funny, 4 = very funny) during the scanning procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mean ± SD for ratings across joke types and baselines; analyze with one-way repeated-measures ANOVA and Bonferroni post hoc tests to identify which joke conditions differ from unfunny conditions. Check for main effects of sex/gender and interactions (e.g., joke type × sex/gender).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main effects and interaction statistical threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The activation threshold of main effects and interaction was set at p < 0.05 FWE (family-wise error rate) corrected for multiple comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whole-brain or appropriate correction to control FWE when reporting main effects and interactions; report Z-scores, voxel counts, MNI coordinates and Brodmann areas for significant clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple main effects / ROI thresholding
rubrics_metrics.description: The activation threshold for simple main effects was set at p < 0.05 FWE for multiple comparisons within five contiguous voxels using in eight predefined ROIs for each type of jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply small-volume correction (SVC) within predefined ROIs and require at least five contiguous voxels to declare simple main-effect significance; indicate which ROIs were predefined and note any special notation (e.g., midbrain ROIs indicated by italics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-volume correction (SVC) with 10-mm sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses used SVC and a 10-mm sphere on the ROI; voxel-wise significance reported at p < 0.05 FWE using SVC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hypothesis-driven ROI tests, use SVC with an explicit sphere radius (here 10 mm) and report voxel-wise corrected p-values, Z-scores, and voxel counts within the SVC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined ROIs and anatomical labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses focused on predefined ROIs including anterior prefrontal cortex (aPFC, BA 10), dorsal prefrontal cortex (dPFC, BA 8/9), temporoparietal junction (TPJ, BA 39), parahippocampal gyrus (PHG), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC, BA 11), supplementary motor area (SMA, BA 6), amygdala, and midbrain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ROIs anatomically (BA labels, MNI coordinates) and report side, voxel counts, coordinates, and Z-scores for ROI activations; indicate special functional interpretations (e.g., aPFC cognitive flexibility, OFC reward coding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-related design comparing joke types to baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Used event-related fMRI to identify neural substrates by comparing BJs (bridging-inference), EJs (exaggeration), and AJs (ambiguity) to their corresponding non-joke baselines (BS, ES, AS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include corresponding non-joke baselines for each joke type to isolate humor-specific processing (incongruity detection/resolution, appreciation, expression); contrast each joke type against its baseline and compare across types and groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of joke types
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes were categorized into Bridging-inference jokes (BJ), Exaggeration jokes (EJ), and Ambiguity jokes (AJ), each with a corresponding baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theoretically motivated categories (e.g., BJs require contextual bridging/ToM inference; EJs involve distorting incongruity; AJs involve semantic ambiguity) when designing stimuli and interpreting network activations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-series analysis and hemodynamic response characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: A time-series analysis was performed to determine the response to the different contrast types in each region, averaged across participants; the hemodynamic response peaked at approximately 6 s after stimulus onset and returned to baseline at ~12 s followed by a shallow undershoot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract averaged BOLD time courses (PSTH) per ROI and per group, plot mean responses (e.g., women vs men) and interpret peak amplitude, latency, and shape; use these curves to compare magnitude (effect size) and temporal dynamics between groups and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peak voxel extraction from beta values
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant signal changes for brain regions were visualized by extracting the peak voxels of the regions from the beta values and extracting average time courses for different joke types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify peak voxels within significant clusters (from beta maps), extract their beta values/time courses for visualization and quantitative comparisons across conditions and groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Within-group variance analysis using 95% CI of PSTH
rubrics_metrics.description: Within-group variance was examined by calculating the 95% confidence interval through the PSTH of time-series analysis using signal changes for brain regions by extracting peak voxels from beta values; larger CI area indicates greater within-group variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and visualize 95% CIs around mean PSTHs for each group to assess heterogeneity in responses; summarize frequencies/percentages of participants meeting ROI activation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-level participant ROI activation criterion and group frequency reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The coordinates of a given ROI in first-level analysis for each participant were examined using SVC with a 10-mm sphere; results for participants meeting this ROI activation criterion were summed by group and reported as frequency (W, M) and percentage (W%, M%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the per-participant ROI activation threshold/criterion, then report how many participants in each group showed activation in each ROI (both count and percentage) to convey prevalence of effects across subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random-group (pseudorandom exchange) analysis as a chance-check
rubrics_metrics.description: Performed random-grouping analysis by pseudorandomly exchanging 1–6 participants between the male and female groups in 'modes' A–F, repeating mixed ANOVAs three times per mode (total 18 analyses) to check whether observed sex/gender differences could be due to chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement permutation-like or pseudorandom exchange procedures across multiple exchange sizes, run the same group × condition statistical tests repeatedly, and report number of significant interactions across permutations as an empirical check on chance-driven group differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analyses: ANOVA framework and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral ratings analyzed with one-way repeated-measures ANOVA (e.g., F(5,125)=184.25, p<0.001, ηp2=0.88) and mixed ANOVAs used for group × joke-type analyses; post hoc Bonferroni tests used for pairwise comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate within-subjects and mixed-model ANOVAs for condition and group effects, report full statistics (F, df, p, partial eta squared), and apply Bonferroni correction for multiple post hoc pairwise tests on behavioral measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-comparisons control and cluster/extent criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple-comparisons control was achieved using FWE correction; simple main effects additionally required significance within five contiguous voxels in ROIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine voxel-wise FWE correction with minimal cluster/extent thresholds (e.g., five contiguous voxels) inside ROIs to limit false positives; explicitly state both correction method and extent requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting conventions for neuroimaging results
rubrics_metrics.description: Report region name, Brodmann area, number of voxels, MNI coordinates (x,y,z), and Z-score for each significant effect or interaction (see Tables 1–3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard reporting: label anatomy and BA, provide voxel counts and peak coordinates, and include statistical values (Z-scores or t/F values) and side (L/R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive mapping of networks to joke processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Map observed activations to functional interpretations and networks (e.g., temporoparietal–mesocortical–motor network for BJs, frontal-mesolimbic for EJs, frontal-paralimbic for AJs) to explain cognitive vs affective vs laughter processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting results, relate ROI activations to theoretical constructs (e.g., ToM, reward coding, motor expression of laughter) and to the tri-component theory of humor; be cautious about reverse inference and consider alternative functional attributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of theoretical background and prior findings to guide ROI selection
rubrics_metrics.description: ROI selection and interpretation were informed by prior literature (e.g., aPFC linked to cognitive flexibility and episodic retrieval; OFC to reward evaluation; SMA to expressive laughter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground ROI hypotheses in prior studies and theory (tri-component theory of humor, ToM literature, reward circuitry) and cite relevant work when selecting and interpreting ROIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect-size-related visualization and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-series analysis was used to analyze magnitude of BOLD signal changes (i.e., effect size) associated with each joke type by averaging responses across participants and comparing peak amplitudes between groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use averaged PSTHs and peak amplitude comparisons to convey effect sizes of conditions and group differences; complement voxelwise statistical maps with time-course plots to aid interpretation.
